title: Assemble kept collection members by boolean union
description: Merge the kept members of a collection (CRAW-12) into one mesh. Add a `merge_collection.dsl` pattern (or a small node if the graph gets unwieldy) that aligns each kept member to the first (rigid registration: PCA pre-alignment + ICP over sampled points, as an `align_to_mesh` node; manual override via transform_geometry literals), then chains mesh_boolean UNION in order, tagging every face with its source member via CRAW-13 provenance so the result can be tinted per scan and the user can see which generation each region came from. This is REFACTOR-PLAN-2 D7 (loaded models as boolean operands) done on real data. Handle non-watertight members by reporting, not repairing (repair is a separate ticket if needed). Related: MESH-50 (unwelded duplicates after mesh_boolean) will compound over a ten-member union chain.
definition-of-done: 1. Two crawfish scans: `merge_collection` produces one closed mesh in mesh-boolean scene, tinted by source member (screenshot). 2. align_to_mesh reduces mean nearest-point distance between two scans by at least 5x versus unaligned. 3. All ten members (kept) union in under 5 minutes on the dev machine or the ticket documents which stage dominates. 4. Non-manifold input is reported with member name and defect counts instead of a crash. 5. Build checkstyle-green.
testing-plan: 1. Unit: align_to_mesh on a torus and a rotated/translated copy recovers the transform within 1e-3. 2. Unit: union of three tagged cubes carries three member tags. 3. run-scene mesh-boolean with merge_collection on ~/crawfish (two members, then all kept).
todos: align_to_mesh node (PCA + ICP) with reusable buffers
merge_collection.dsl pattern reading collection.dsl keep flags
Per-member provenance tags through the union chain
Manifold/watertight check with a readable report
Timing record for the full ten-member union
unknowns: Whether union is the right operator at all when scans overlap almost completely (may want per-label part selection from members instead -- see CRAW-17)
Whether Manifold handles ~10M-triangle unions in memory
